Rule: All three given matrix cells contain the same filled black square, so the missing cell should also be the filled black square.
All three given cells are identical, showing a plus sign inside a circle, so the missing cell should be the same.
Across each row the filled right triangle is mirrored left-right, while down each column it remains unchanged, so the missing cell matches B.
Going right mirrors the figure left–right and going down mirrors it top–bottom, so the missing cell must be A flipped both ways, i.e. the circle with the upper-left quadrant removed.
Moving down a column reflects the figure vertically (A bottom-right triangle becomes C top-right triangle), so B's bottom-left square flips to a top-left square.
Moving down mirrors the diagonal horizontally, so mirroring B gives a backslash diagonal with the shaded triangle in the lower-left half.

Across each row the 3/4 circle is mirrored left-right (cut-out SE→SW, so NE→NW), while down each column it changes from solid to outline with the cut-out flipped vertically; the missing cell is the unfilled shape with the notch in the upper-left.
Across each row the outer shape changes from circle to square while the half-black/half-white arrangement is preserved (left white, right black).
Across each row the same shape changes from outline to filled, and down each column the shape changes from octagon to square while preserving fill state.

Across each row the inner concentric circle becomes an outlined square, and down each column a filled black square is added; so the missing cell has one circle containing an outlined square with a black square inside.
Across each row the inner black diamond is removed, while down each column the outer shape changes from heart to octagon.
Across the row the two outermost concentric circles are removed, and down the column the two innermost are removed, so applying both leaves only the middle circle.

Cells are identical within each row, and the number of nested squares increases by one down each column (row/column 1 = one square, row/column 2 = two nested squares, row/column 3 = three nested squares), so the missing cell must contain three nested squares matching G and H.

The outer square increases by one size step across each row and down each column while the filled inner square remains unchanged, so the missing cell is the largest outer square with the same filled center.

Each cell's diamond count equals its row number times its column number (1/2/3 across × 1/2/3 down), so the missing r3c3 cell needs 3×3 = 9 diamonds; option 4 has nine diamonds (option 6 is a distractor with unrotated squares).
Across each row the side-by-side circles increase 1→2→3 while down each column the stacked circles increase 1→2→3, so the missing cell must combine three across with three down.

Each step right adds a dot to the next star tip (upper-right then lower-right), and each step down adds a dot (upper-left then lower-left), so the missing cell must contain the star with all five tips dotted.

Across each row the black rectangle's width steps 1, 2, 3 units while its height stays fixed, and down each column the height steps 1, 2, 3 units; the missing bottom-right cell must be the 3-by-3 large square.

In each row the circle shifts around the diamond by one step (top row: upper-left → above → upper-right; bottom row: lower-left → below → lower-right; columns likewise advance downward), so the missing cell needs the diamond above-left with the circle to its lower-right.

The matrix is symmetric under transposition with the inner 2x2 reflected across its own main diagonal (top-right swaps with bottom-left); the diagonal cells fill progressively, so the missing cell has off-diagonal subcells black and main-diagonal subcells white.

Across each row the same pair of shapes goes from touching tip-to-tip (column 1), to overlapped/merged into one composite (column 2), to reversed and separated by a central vertical gap (column 3); since row 3 uses stars and a star is left-right symmetric, the missing cell is two upright stars separated by a gap.

Each column fixes the horizontal relation (single, touching, separated) and each row fixes the vertical relation (single, touching, separated), so the missing cell must have four diamonds separated in both directions.

Across each row a diamond is added extending the bottom row leftward, while down each column the upper right-column diamonds are removed one by one, so the missing cell contains only the three bottom-row diamonds.

Each cell equals the pixel union of the first cell of its row and the first cell of its column (moving right blackens the inner top-middle then top-left cell; moving down blackens the inner middle-left then top-left cell), so the missing cell has the whole inner first row and first column black with only the central 2x2 left white.
Each row repeats the same figure across the three columns, while each column goes star, heart, octagon from top to bottom.
Each row and column contains one filled black circle, diamond, and triangle in a cyclic Latin-square order, so the missing cell must be a filled black circle.

Each row and column contains exactly one cell with circle-only, one with triangle+circle, and one with triangle+circle+square (a Latin square of set sizes 1, 2, 3), so the missing cell must be circle-only.
Each row keeps the same inner symbol (plus, star, heart) and each column keeps the same outer shape (circle, diamond, square), so the missing cell is a heart inside a square.

Each row keeps the same central shape (square, diamond, octagon) while each column applies the same modifier: column 1 surrounds it with a circle outline, column 2 cuts a white circle from it, and column 3 places two black dots above and below the solid shape; so the missing cell is a solid octagon with dots above and below.

Each row contains the inner symbols circle, plus, and triangle exactly once in a shifted Latin-square order, while the number of concentric outer squares decreases by row (3 in row 1, 2 in row 2, 1 in row 3), so the missing cell must be a single square containing a circle.

The inner filled symbol (plus, square, heart) and the outer treatment (four dots, circle outline, matching self-outline) each cycle as a Latin square; the missing cell lies on the four-dots diagonal and needs the square inner symbol.
Each row and column cycles the inner shape (square, diamond, circle) and the figure type (filled-only, outline-only, outline+filled combined); the missing cell must be a filled-only diamond.
Outer shape (circle/octagon/square) and inner bar pattern (vertical/horizontal/both) each cycle as Latin squares across rows and columns, so the missing cell is an octagon with a vertical bar only.

The central shape (square/diamond/circle) and the attachment style (detached small squares, diagonal corner lines, cardinal lines) each cycle as a Latin square across rows and columns, so the missing cell must be a square center with diagonal corner attachments.
Each row and column contains one fully filled star, one filled star with a white central pentagon, and one outlined star with a black central pentagon; the missing cell must be the fully filled star.
Across each row and down each column the shape cycles square→triangle→star (each appearing once) while the item count cycles through 3, 4, 5; the missing cell must therefore contain 3 triangles.

In every row and column the third cell is the union of the first two cells' triangles, so the missing cell must combine G (left+up) and H (down+right), equivalently C (left+right) and F (up+down), giving all four orientations.
In each row the third cell is the overlay/union of the first two cells (and likewise down each column), so the missing cell must combine the plus, circle, square, and X.

In each row (and each column) the third figure is the union of the diamond positions in the first two figures, so the missing cell is G ∪ H = C ∪ F, which fills all eight outer ring positions with no center diamond.

In every column the top cell is the overlay (union) of the middle and bottom cells (and likewise each row's left cell is the overlay of the other two), so C = F overlaid with the missing cell, leaving just the outer square.

In each row and column the middle cell is the union of the two outer cells, so the missing cell must supply only the inner diamond (with the universal central dot) and no outer square, cross, or corner triangles.

Each cell contains two of four features (corner squares, circle, border, plus), and the third cell in every row and column is the XOR/symmetric difference of the first two (shared features cancel, unshared features remain), giving corner squares + plus.

In every row and column the third figure is the XOR (symmetric difference) of the first two: segments shared by the first two cancel out, while unshared segments are kept, so the missing cell must contain all six segments (square plus both diagonals).

In each row the third panel pairs the upper outline shape of the first panel with the lower filled shape of the second panel (equivalently down each column the top shape repeats row 1 and the bottom shape repeats row 2), so the missing cell is an outline triangle above a filled square.

In every row and column the third figure is the intersection of the first two (only shared triangular points are kept); G points only left and H only right, so they share no point and only the plain central square remains.
The third cell in each row and column is the pixel intersection of the first two cells, keeping only black areas common to both.

Counting each up-triangle as +1 and each down-triangle as -1, the third cell of every row (and the bottom cell of every column) is the algebraic sum of the other two with up/down pairs cancelling; G(+2)+H(-1)=+1, i.e. one up-triangle.
Across each row the figure rotates 90° clockwise, and down each column one triangle is replaced by three smaller triangles at the original triangle's vertices.
Moving right rotates the triangle 45° clockwise and moving down rotates it 45° counterclockwise, so the missing cell rotates back to the same orientation as A.

Across each row, concentric square outlines are converted into alternating filled bands starting with black on the outside; down each column the number of concentric squares drops from five to three, so C becomes a black-white-black filled pattern.
Across the row alternate annuli are filled black, and down the column every other concentric boundary is dropped, so the remaining filled bands merge into one outer black annulus with a white center.
A is the union of B and C, so the missing cell is their intersection: the square and diamond have no overlap, leaving an empty panel.
The left column is solid black and the right column is hatched; moving down flips the shaded triangle vertically, so the missing right-column cell is the hatched upper-left triangle.

Across each row the three-quarter circle is mirrored left-right while keeping the same fill, and down each column it is mirrored top-bottom and changes from solid to striped, so the missing cell is striped with the upper-left quadrant absent.
The number of polygon sides increases by 1 across each row and by 2 down each column, so the missing cell must be a hexagon.
Across each row the fill changes from vertical stripes to solid black while the shape stays the same, and down each column the shape changes from circle to heart while the fill stays the same.
A→B rotates the whole three-triangle arrangement 90° clockwise, while A→C rotates only the triangle orientations 90° clockwise, so the missing cell has B's positions with downward-pointing triangles.
B is A reflected left-right and C is A reflected top-bottom, so the missing cell is A rotated 180 degrees.
Move right by rotating the figure 90° clockwise and move down by changing the triangle to the corresponding octagon; rotating the flat-topped octagon 90° leaves it unchanged.

The three concentric-square patterns cycle as a Latin square, so each row and column contains one thin-outlined black-centered figure, one solid-black outer figure with a white center, and one thin-bordered thick-black figure with a white center.
The number of horizontal squares increases by one across each row and down each column, so the missing cell needs five horizontal squares.

In each row the third cell's triangle count is the sum of the first two (1+2=3, 2+4=6, 3+6=9), while fill color alternates in a checkerboard (outline/filled), so the missing cell needs 9 outline triangles.
Across each row the horizontal lines increase from 1 to 3 while down each column the vertical lines increase from 1 to 3, so the missing cell must contain three vertical and three horizontal lines.
The count of shapes drops by one across each row and down each column (4-3-2 / 3-2-1 / 2-1-0), while circles and squares alternate in a checkerboard, leaving the final cell empty.

Columns fix the shape (triangles, circles, squares); each row multiplies the count by the row number (row n has n, 2n, 3n items), and fill alternates in a checkerboard (outline/filled), so the missing cell needs 9 outline squares.
In row r the cells contain r, 2r, 3r filled triangles, with orientation alternating down/up/down across the checkerboard, so the missing cell needs 9 filled downward triangles.

Across columns the solid-black region retreats leftward (black→diagonal stripes) and down rows it retreats upward; within each cell the column and row contributions add (black=0, stripes=1, cross/plus=2), so column 3 plus row 3 yields the cross pattern everywhere.

Each row keeps one shape (octagon, circle, diamond) while across the columns the smaller copy moves from separate beside the large shape, to overlapping its right edge, to concentric inside it with the dot centered; the missing cell needs concentric diamonds.

Across each row, the two same-shaped figures go from separated with the dot between them (col 1), to overlapping with the dot inside the smaller figure (col 2), to concentric with the dot in the center (col 3); rows use circles, squares, then octagons.
Columns fix the shape (triangles, circles, squares) while the count equals row index times column index, so the missing square cell needs 3×3 = 9 squares.
Each row and column contains one triangle, one circle, and one square, and also one small, one medium, and one large figure; the missing cell must be a medium-sized circle.

Each cell is the union of a row pattern (row1 none, row2 upper-left quarter, row3 left half) and a column pattern (col1 none, col2 upper-left quarter, col3 upper half); the missing cell unions the left half with the upper half, leaving only the lower-right quarter white.
The notch rotates 90° clockwise across each row and down each column, so the missing cell must have the notch opening to the right.
Cells are identical along each NW-SE diagonal, so the missing main-diagonal cell must match A and E (the upward-pointing triangle).
Moving right or down advances the triangle one step clockwise through the orientation sequence up → upper-right → right → lower-right → down, so the missing cell is the downward triangle.

In each row the middle single circle is the union of the two notched circles in the left cell, and the right cell is the left cell with the two circles swapped (notches facing outward instead of inward); applying this to row 3 swaps G's step-notches to the outer sides.

Each row keeps one border style (row 1 dashed corners, row 2 solid square, row 3 double square) while the inner symbol cycles star→trefoil→diamond shifted one position per row, so the missing cell is the double-square border with the trefoil.
Each row and column cycles the three shapes (star, heart, octagon) and the three fills (outline, hatched, solid) one step, so the missing cell is a hatched star.

Each row and column contains 1, 2 and 3 triangles, exactly one black-filled cell and exactly one right-pointing cell; right-pointing figures are the corresponding up-pointing arrangements rotated 90° clockwise, so the missing cell is two outlined right-pointing triangles stacked vertically.
Fill pattern (checkerboard/blank/diagonal) and bar configuration (vertical/horizontal/both) each form a Latin square across rows and columns, so the missing cell must be blank with both bars.

In each row the three outline triangles in column 3 are the column-2 trio rotated so they point the same direction as the solid triangle in column 1 (right, left, down); row 3 needs a 180° rotation, giving two down-triangles on top and one centered below.

The left edge cycles through curved, slanted, and vertical in every row/column, while the short bottom segment occurs only on the C-E-G anti-diagonal and the missing cell must keep the top edge, so it is the curved-left figure with top edge and no bottom segment.
The object counts form a cyclic Latin square—each row and column contains 2, 3, and 4 items exactly once—so the missing cell must contain exactly 2 objects (two arcs).

In each row (and each column), the third figure is the XOR/symmetric difference of the first two: unit squares present in both cancel, leaving those present in exactly one; so G XOR H cancels the shared top-right square and leaves the bottom-left plus bottom-right squares, i.e. a bottom horizontal domino.
In every row and every column, the third panel is the pixel-wise union (logical OR) of the first two panels, so the missing panel has all nine triangles filled black.
In each row and column, the third cell contains only the shapes common to the first two cells (intersection), so the missing cell is G ∩ H = {triangle} only.

In each row and each column, the first/upper cell is the disjoint union of the region-types (empty, horizontal-only, vertical-only, cross-hatched) found in the other two cells, so the missing cell must contain only a vertical-striped region.
Across each row and down each column the polygon gains two sides, so the missing cell must be a 12-sided polygon.

In every row and column the total number of sides of the third cell equals the sum of the totals of the first two (e.g., 3+4=7, 6+3=9, and 4+3=7 confirming H is a heptagon), so the missing cell must total 9+7=16 sides.
Each step right or down adds two points to the star, so the missing figure must have 12 points.

Counting sides/points, in each row and column one figure's count equals the sum of the other two; the missing count is 8, and since row 3 already has its single plain polygon (G), the missing figure must be the 8-point star.

Encode the notch-opening direction in Z4 (right=0, up=1, left=2, down=3 going counterclockwise); in every row and every column the third cell's value equals the sum mod 4 of the first two (e.g., down+up=right, left+left=right), so the missing cell must open to the right.
In every row and column, the first two cells are merged and each upward triangle cancels one downward triangle; the uncanceled remainder forms the third cell, leaving a single upward triangle.

Reading across each row, one symbol is added per cell so totals go 1-2-3 / 4-5-6 / 7-8-9, and from the first to the third cell of every row exactly one circle and one cross are added (net +1 O, +1 X); thus the missing cell is H plus one circle in the last empty (bottom-right) position, giving 5 circles and 4 crosses.
The number of perched birds increases by one across each row and down each column, so the missing cell must contain five birds.
